# FrameLane

> Hosted, versioned video projects that a person and an AI agent build and edit together.

Connect the MCP server at https://mcp.framelane.io/mcp and sign in, or send an API key as a Bearer token. Read the handbook first, then the skill that fits the job. Each skill below is served as markdown without a key; on the MCP server a workflow skill is also a prompt, and every skill is the `get_capabilities` section `skills.<name>`. The installable bundle is https://github.com/ITIShq/framelane-skills.

## Skills

- [handbook](https://api.framelane.io/v1/skills/handbook): FrameLane's shared contract for building, previewing, reviewing, handing off and exporting a versioned video project over MCP. Read it before the first composition in any FrameLane workflow.
- [brief-to-video](https://api.framelane.io/v1/skills/brief-to-video): Assemble a narrated, editable FrameLane video from a written brief and the user's own media. Use when someone hands over a brief or script plus footage, images or a voiceover.
- [caption](https://api.framelane.io/v1/skills/caption): Add or revise timed captions in FrameLane from a real transcript. Use when a video needs subtitles, burned-in captions or word-by-word caption styling.
- [explainer](https://api.framelane.io/v1/skills/explainer): Explain an idea with motion graphics in FrameLane, silent or with supplied narration. Use for concept, process, comparison or how-it-works explainers built from text, shapes and simple diagrams.
- [localize](https://api.framelane.io/v1/skills/localize): Create a translated locale variant of a FrameLane project that preserves meaning and readability, with honest caption timing and script checks. Use when someone wants a video translated or adapted for another language or market.
- [onboard](https://api.framelane.io/v1/skills/onboard): Introduce FrameLane's workflows and, when someone wants to try editing, create a real, editable sample project. Use when someone is new to FrameLane or asks what it can do.
- [reframe](https://api.framelane.io/v1/skills/reframe): Create faithful versions of a FrameLane project for another aspect ratio. Use when someone needs 9:16, 1:1 or 16:9 variants of an existing video.
- [review](https://api.framelane.io/v1/skills/review): Review a FrameLane project from server-rendered frames and lint, and repair it with targeted edits when asked. Use when asked to check, critique, QA or fix an existing video project.
- [shorts](https://api.framelane.io/v1/skills/shorts): Cut captioned vertical shorts from real footage in FrameLane. Use when someone has a long video recording, such as an interview, talk or podcast, and wants 9:16 clips.
- [styles](https://api.framelane.io/v1/skills/styles): Named visual styles for FrameLane videos, such as dark keynote, Swiss motion, kinetic type or silent film. Use when a brief asks for a stylized look or names a style, before the first composition.
- [talking-head](https://api.framelane.io/v1/skills/talking-head): Clean up a talking-head recording in FrameLane: remove ums, stutters, false starts, retakes, mistakes and dead air by transcript, then add titles, captions and B-roll. Use when someone asks to clean up or polish their recording.
- [teaser](https://api.framelane.io/v1/skills/teaser): Build a short branded launch teaser in FrameLane. Use for a product or feature launch, an event or an announcement with one clear promise and one next action.

## Reference

- [Agent skills](https://docs.framelane.io/agent-skills/overview): installing the bundle, the MCP prompts and the `get_capabilities` sections
- [MCP server](https://docs.framelane.io/mcp/overview): connecting, the tools and their errors
- [Capabilities](https://api.framelane.io/v1/capabilities): the machine-readable catalog, no key needed
- [Skill manifest](https://api.framelane.io/v1/skills): every skill with its sha256
